items.title: Fibre products of affine formal algebraic spaces over a separated base are affine, and McQuillan in the McQuillan case

items.difficulty_reason: For morphisms of formal algebraic spaces into a separated base, the lemma asserts three things: that the fibre product of two affine formal algebraic spaces is affine, that it is McQuillan when both are, and that in the McQuillan case with the three rings named the fibre product corresponds to the completed tensor product (statement lines 3702-3717). The proof writes the two spaces as filtered colimits of affine schemes, so that the fibre product is the colimit of the fibre products of the stages, and those are affine because the base is separated; this gives the first assertion (proof lines 3719-3724). For the second, it writes the stages as spectra of quotients by the ideals of definition and observes that the morphism from the fibre product of two stages into the product of the two spectra is a closed immersion, which verifies the defining condition of the McQuillan type (proof lines 3724-3734). For the third, it identifies the fibre product of two stages with the spectrum of the tensor product of the two quotients over the quotient of the base, so that the ring associated with the fibre product is the completed tensor product (proof lines 3734-3741). The claim is H2: the three assertions are obtained from one colimit description, and the second and third each require a separate identification of the stages, the first by a closed immersion and the second by a tensor product of quotients.
